title: November flow gave no clear added March forecast gain beyond a trend at Mackenzie in 24 winters from 1995 to 2019
abstract: We tested whether prior November flow improves March log-flow forecasts beyond a linear time trend at the Mackenzie Arctic Red River gauge. ArcticGRO v20261104 gave 24 approved test winters in 1995-2019. Each fit used earlier eligible winters only. Adding November reduced mean squared error by 6.61%, with conditional 95% three-position block limits of -35.33% to 37.27%. RMSE fell from 0.13929 to 0.13461 log units. The fitted November slope cut error by 70.28% against a unit slope with a trend, but that reference had much higher error than the trend alone. Five-position blocks and last-15-winter fits gave no clear added gain beyond time. This separate basin and national agency test extends earlier Siberian work, with the same ArcticGRO compilation. It does not establish a physical cause or prove no useful autumn information. Short records, regulation, final revised data and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Original code, aggregate scores and draws, source hashes, an arithmetic audit and a figure support reproduction. Source and record-level tables remain external.

display.caption: Forecast error gains at Mackenzie in 24 approved winters from 1995 to 2019. Lines show conditional 95% paired three-position block limits. The primary comparison is November plus trend against trend.
